acceptanceCriteria: An implementer attempt that produces no new commit is treated as a failed attempt, not a reviewable candidate
No reviewer is ever dispatched against a candidate commit equal to the base commit
The resulting failure names the real cause, that the implementer reported success while committing nothing, so an operator is not left reading an empty review
A reviewer brief can never be built with baseCommit equal to candidateCommit; the brief builder fails closed on that pair exactly as it already does on a missing candidate
Regression coverage drives an implementer that exits success without committing, and asserts no review job is dispatched and no budget is spent on one
deliverables: src/campaign/supervisor.ts around the candidateCommit derivation: stop substituting the base commit for a missing implementer commit, and gate reviewer dispatch on a genuinely new candidate
Fail-closed guard in buildTaskBrief for a reviewer brief whose base and candidate commits are equal
Tests covering the silent-no-commit implementer path end to end
title: Never dispatch a reviewer against a candidate commit equal to the base commit
verification: A campaign whose implementer exits success without committing dispatches no reviewer and reports the missing commit as the failure
